name: Dev Container Development Certificates
description: Enables trusted HTTPS in Dev Containers by preparing certificate trust infrastructure and installing companion VS Code extensions that automatically generate, trust, and transfer ASP.NET and Aspire compatible development certificates from the host machine. Add to your devcontainer.json: "features": { "ghcr.io/dnegstad/devcontainer-dev-certs/devcontainer-dev-certs:1": {} }

trustNss.description: Install NSS tools (certutil) for Chromium/Firefox certificate trust inside the container

sslCertDirs.description: Colon-separated system CA certificate directories to include in SSL_CERT_DIR alongside the dev-certs trust directory. The default covers paths from several Linux distributions; directories that don't exist are filtered out at install time. Override this if your base image uses non-standard paths; explicit values are used as-is.

generateDotNetCert.description: Auto-generate the ASP.NET Core / Aspire compatible HTTPS development certificate. Set to false to skip generation (for example when only syncing user-provided certificates).

syncUserCertificates.description: Allow the host extension to sync user-provided certificates (configured via the devcontainerDevCerts.userCertificates VS Code setting) into this container.

syncContainerCert.description: Opt in to reverse-sync: when this container already has a valid ASP.NET HTTPS dev certificate (e.g. produced by `dotnet dev-certs https` baked into the image), the workspace extension pushes it to the host extension to trust on this host machine. The host independently re-validates the certificate, restricts SANs to local addresses by default (override with devcontainerDevCerts.allowNonLocalContainerCertSans), and prompts before adding it to the host OS trust store. Setting this to true ALSO implicitly overrides generateDotNetCert for this container — the container becomes the source of its own dev cert, so we don't ask the host to generate a different one and send it back. User-managed certificates are unaffected. Gated host-side by the existing devcontainerDevCerts.generateDotNetCert and devcontainer-dev-certs.autoProvision VS Code settings — if the user has opted out of managed dev certs on their host, the push is rejected. No fallback: if no valid cert is found in the container, the push is skipped entirely.

extraCertDestinations.description: Comma-separated additional directories to write cert artifacts to. Each entry: <abs-dir>[=<format>] where format is pem|key|pem-bundle|pfx|all (defaults to all). Every synced cert is written under the directory as {name}.{pem,key,pfx} (and/or {name}-bundle.pem). Example: /etc/nginx/certs=pem,/var/myapp.
